problem: Existing VLN methods, limited by scarce navigation data, cannot fully learn commonsense relationships between rooms and landmarks (e.g., which objects typically appear in which room type), which are needed for environmental understanding.
motivation: Commonsense about room layouts and typical landmarks helps grounding instructions and reasoning in unseen environments. Large models (ChatGPT, BLIP-2, Stable Diffusion) hold open-world knowledge that can compensate for scarce navigation data, at both the textual and visual level.
key_idea: Inject room-type and landmark commonsense from BLIP-2 (room type per panorama), ChatGPT (typical landmarks per room type) and Stable Diffusion (commonsense images) into VLN via text and visual commonsense layout learning modules.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations can be cited. The abstract suggests that complementing the agent with both linguistic and visual commonsense from foundation models improves environment understanding and generalization on REVERIE, R2R and SOON.
method: Room-type recognition: BLIP-2 predicts the room type for each panoramic image.
Landmark knowledge: ChatGPT infers the most common landmarks for each room type, giving textual commonsense.
Visual commonsense generation: Stable Diffusion generates commonsense-based images to enhance the agent's visual perception.
Text Commonsense Layout Learning Module: helps the agent learn environmental commonsense from the linguistic side.
Visual Commonsense Layout Learning Module: helps the agent learn environmental commonsense from the visual side.

setting.backbone: ViTeC (learned navigation policy) with BLIP-2, ChatGPT and Stable Diffusion as commonsense sources; exact policy backbone not stated in the abstract
setting.training_data: Standard REVERIE, R2R and SOON training data plus generated commonsense (room types, landmarks, images); scale not stated
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (discrete viewpoints), plus generated commonsense text and images
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (likely, not stated in the abstract)
setting.simulator: Matterport3D simulator (likely, not stated in the abstract)

results: The abstract claims strong performance on REVERIE, R2R and SOON and good generalization in complex environments, but gives no numbers or named baselines.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so quantitative results and ablations could not be checked.
Depends on external large models (ChatGPT, BLIP-2, Stable Diffusion), which adds preprocessing cost and possible noise or hallucination in the commonsense.
